page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare-metal server in the Bare Metal NVMe family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 4345P processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a base clock frequency of 3.9 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 123.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM (7.71 GB per core). For persistent data storage, the server is bundled with 3,890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and networking is provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration does not include a GPU accelerator.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-thread processing capabilities. The platform scores in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core stress-ng tests (4,638.98) and Geekbench single-core evaluations (3,400.0). Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression (50.05 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (22.26 GB/sec) also achieve top-tier performance, alongside Geekbench image and text processing. Multi-core performance scales moderately, yielding average results in stress-ng (36,336.78), PassMark CPU score (38,156.62), and Geekbench multi-core (15,781.0), as expected from an 8-core configuration.

The system balances fast memory access with local I/O performance. PassMark memory testing registers in the top 10% (3,301.4), though large uncached write bandwidth measures at a lower 21.89 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput achieves 33.37 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 35.96 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning inference, the high clock rate and DDR5 speed deliver top-tier throughput on small models, generating 414.79 tokens per second on a 135M parameter LLM.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a fast 8-core processor, high-capacity DDR5 RAM, and 3.8 TB of NVMe storage yields strong cost efficiency for workloads that benefit from single-thread speed and low-latency storage rather than massive multi-socket core counts. This hardware profile suits relational database engines, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD build environments, and moderate web serving pipelines requiring dedicated hardware access.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare-metal server driven by an AMD EPYC 4345P processor operating at 3.9 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 123.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory and 3,890 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, this server delivers dedicated single-tenant performance without a GPU. Benchmark testing reveals top-tier single-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and file compression tests, paired with strong memory speeds and top-tier execution for small-model LLM inference. Multi-threaded processing scores in the median range due to its balanced 8-core architecture, while uncached memory write throughput presents a slight bottleneck under heavy write loads. Bundling high-capacity NVMe drives with high-frequency DDR5 memory, the server offers efficient compute density for dedicated database servers, Redis caches, CI/CD build pipelines, and performance-sensitive web application backends.
